background.text: A year ago, I would have said, you're right, Mike, but now here we are, and we are faced with a scenario where people are looking at Donald Trump as he is gaining more momentum and more support, many of whom, one of the reasons they like him is because they kind of think he is what you actually are, and many reasons he's become so successful, so much traction is because people have said, it's so crazy, it just might work.

If I had to bet today, I would bet that Hillary Clinton is the Democratic nominee, and on the Republican side, it'll probably be one of the more traditional candidates. I always thought, as did a lot of other people, that it would be Jeb Bush. Rubio seems to be doing better at the time. If you ask yourself who of all of these candidates can run the railroad, who of all of these candidates can execute, can direct a four-million-person organization, Hillary can argue that she can. And on the Republican side, Bush and Kasich both were governors and have a lot of executive experience. If you don't have the executive experience, then it's much tougher to win. It's much harder to run the railroad.
